recommendations:
TOP RESTAURANTS
Sukiyabashi Jiro, Sushi, 20,000-30,000 JPY (14,000-21,000 INR) per person, must-order dish: Omakase.
Narisawa, Japanese, 15,000-25,000 JPY (10,500-17,500 INR) per person, must-order dish: Satoyama.
Tofuya Ukai, Tofu, 5,000-10,000 JPY (3,500-7,000 INR) per person, must-order dish: Tofu Katsu.
Ichiran Shibuya, Ramen, 890-1,000 JPY (620-700 INR) per person, must-order dish: Tonkotsu Ramen.
Asakaze Nakamura, Kaiseki, 10,000-20,000 JPY (7,000-14,000 INR) per person, must-order dish: Seasonal Kaiseki.

TOP ATTRACTIONS
Shibuya Crossing, experience busiest intersection, best time to go: evening, entry fee: free.
Meiji Shrine, dedicated to Emperor Meiji, best time to go: morning, entry fee: free.
Tsukiji Outer Market, fresh seafood and sushi, best time to go: morning, entry fee: free.
Tokyo Tower, panoramic views of city, best time to go: sunset, entry fee: 2,060 JPY (1,400 INR).
Asakusa Kannon Temple, ancient Buddhist temple, best time to go: morning, entry fee: 500 JPY (350 INR).

HIDDEN GEMS
Neon Museum, showcases vintage neon signs, located in Shinjuku.
Kappabashi Dougu Street, shopping street for kitchen tools and gadgets, located in Asakusa.
Imperial Palace East Garden, beautiful traditional Japanese garden, located in Chiyoda.

TRAVEL TIPS
Learn basic Japanese customs like bowing and using chopsticks to show respect.
Use Tokyo Metro for best transport, buy a prepaid IC card like Suica or Pasmo.
Be cautious of pickpocketing in crowded areas and train stations, keep valuables secure.
Learn useful phrases like "konnichiwa" (hello) and "arigatou" (thank you).
Carry a portable Wi-Fi hotspot and keep hotel address written in Japanese for safety.

SHOPPING
Ginza Mitsukoshi, department store with high-end goods, price range: 5,000-50,000 JPY (3,500-35,000 INR).
Ameya Yokocho, shopping street with traditional snacks and souvenirs, price range: 500-2,000 JPY (350-1,400 INR).
Don Quijote, discount store with variety of goods, price range: 1,000-10,000 JPY (700-7,000 INR).
